item.title: Cosmic dust chemistry forges peptide building blocks in deep space
item.description: New experiments show that key molecular building blocks for life can form spontaneously on icy dust grains in deep space long before planets emerge from collapsing gas clouds. item.title: Hydrogen sulfide detected in distant gas giant exoplanets for the first time
item.description: Hydrogen sulfide is what makes rotten eggs stink. But the discovery of this gas in the atmospheres of four distant, Jupiter-like planets is turning heads for a pleasant reason: It solves the mystery of how some gas giants form. item.title: JWST study links sulfur rich gas giants to core growth in distant HR 8799 system
item.description: Gas giants are large planets composed mainly of hydrogen and helium with dense cores but no solid surfaces. item.title: Icy cycles may have driven early protocell evolution
item.description: Modern cells rely on intricate molecular machinery and genetic programs to grow and divide, but the earliest protocells were likely simple lipid-bound compartments whose behavior depended mainly on their physical and chemical properties. item.description: A joint team from the Korea Advanced Institute of Science and Technology KAIST and the Unmanned Exploration Laboratory UEL has developed a transformable airless wheel designed to help small rovers access steep lunar pits and lava tubes.
